Goals Go-Live Map
AJMN Talent Suite · Goals 2027

From prototype to a live goals app in SAP Fiori

How to launch the Goals and People apps in the Fiori launchpad, connect them to the HR data that already exists, and give the app its own database. A recommended path, the options, the steps with their exit gates, and the decisions that need an owner.

Prototype: built, tested in a test launchpadConnected to real SAP data: not yetSample data only today
ArchitecturePlatform optionsProcessData mapBest practiceDecisions

The target picture

Users open the apps from the Fiori launchpad. The apps call one goals service. That service reads and writes the existing HR system and keeps only the data nothing else holds in its own database.

What changes on this path:

Choose the platform before building the service

The two apps themselves run on either path. The choice decides where the goals service and its database live.

Recommended

SAP BTP with a CAP service

  • Goals service in SAP CAP, database in SAP HANA Cloud.
  • Launchpad from SAP Build Work Zone; apps in the HTML5 Application Repository.
  • SuccessFactors reached through the Destination service with the user's identity.

Choose when SuccessFactors is the system of record and BTP is available. Fastest to build and keeps ERP untouched.

ABAP front-end server with RAP

  • Apps uploaded with /UI5/UI5_REPOSITORY_LOAD; launchpad already running.
  • Goals service as an ABAP RAP OData service, data in the ABAP system's HANA schema.
  • SuccessFactors called through an SM59 HTTP destination.

Choose when there is no BTP and the Fiori team works in ABAP. Fine for launching the screens now; heavier for the SuccessFactors link.

Extend SuccessFactors only

  • Use SuccessFactors goal plans, route maps and its goal library as they are.
  • The Fiori apps stay a front end over the SuccessFactors APIs, with almost no database of their own.

Choose when the goal rules fit what SuccessFactors can already do. Weights, push down and the cascade view are the features to check first.

The process, in the order it should happen

Each step ends in a gate: a check someone can sign. Durations are planning ranges for a team of four to six and need your own estimate.

11 to 2 weeksPackage is ready

Launch the two apps in the Fiori launchpad

  • Upload both apps (ZAJMN_HR_GOALS, ZAJMN_HR_HOME) or deploy from the project folders.
  • Create the two intents ZAJMNHR-display and ZAJMNGOALS-display: semantic objects, target mappings, tiles.
  • Give both catalogs to the same pilot role, so the links between the apps work.
  • Still sample data. This step proves the screens, navigation, fonts and Arabic in the real launchpad.
Fiori developerBasisLaunchpad admin
Done whenA pilot user opens both apps from tiles, moves between them, and creates a goal in English and Arabic.Next to do. The upload package is built and was run in a test launchpad.
21 to 2 weeksStarts alongside 1

Decide what is not decided

  • Platform path (see above) and who owns the goals service afterwards.
  • System of record for goals, weights and approvals: SuccessFactors or the new service.
  • Open items already marked in the screens: how owner, contributor and team progress combine (D-44), and the review of the 3,204 library goals (D-50).
  • The rule for weights: do they add to 100, per person or per plan, and who may change them.
HR ownerFiori developerIntegration lead
Done whenA one-page decision log is signed, with an owner for each open item.
33 to 4 weeks

Build the goals service and swap out the sample data

  • Model the service on what the screens already do: list and create goals, approve or return, push down, set progress, set weights, read the library.
  • Move the rules out of the browser code (one owner per goal, weights up to 100, only a person's own goals) into the service, so they cannot be bypassed.
  • Replace the in-memory sample data and the sample people table with calls to the service. Replace the English and Arabic word list with UI5 i18n texts.
  • Add role checks from the sign-in, in place of the demo role switcher.
Fiori developerBackend developerSecurity
Done whenThe apps run on the service in the development system with test data, and every rule is enforced by the service.
44 to 6 weeks

Connect the existing data

  • Create an API user and OAuth client in SuccessFactors; set up the destination so calls carry the signed-in user.
  • Read people, managers and org units from Employee Central to build the cascade from the Director General down.
  • Read the goal plan and existing goals; map fields (see the data map); then write goals, progress and weights back.
  • Decide how conflicts resolve (someone edits in SuccessFactors and in the app), cache what is slow, and handle limits and failures with retries and a visible error.
  • Run one reconciliation for the pilot group: counts and sample records compared line by line.
Integration leadHR systemsBackend developer
Done whenThe reconciliation report matches for the pilot group, and a failed sync shows a clear message instead of a blank screen.
52 to 3 weeksRuns alongside 4

Give the app its own database

  • Tables only for what nothing else holds: goal library, translations, activity log, settings, sync state, and weights or links if the goal plan does not carry them.
  • Versioned schema changes, a backup schedule, and a restore that has actually been tried.
  • Retention for the activity log and a rule for personal data in it.
Backend developerBasis or BTP adminData protection
Done whenA restore from backup into a clean system works, and the schema is applied by the delivery pipeline, not by hand.
62 to 3 weeks

Prove it works for every level

  • Automated tests: service rules, the main screens, and the sync, run on every change.
  • Acceptance by role, from Director General to Employee, with real approval chains.
  • Load check at your headcount, a security review, a keyboard and screen-reader pass, and a read of the Arabic by a native speaker.
QAHR ownerSecurityArabic reviewer
Done whenAcceptance is signed for each role, nothing critical is open, and the goal list opens in under two seconds at pilot size.
74 weeks + 4 weeks of support

Pilot, go live, support

  • One division first, with training and a short guide in both languages.
  • Move the same package through quality to production with the transport tool, outside goal-setting deadlines.
  • Watch sync errors, slow screens and sign-in failures on a shared dashboard; keep the last version ready to switch back to.
  • Four weeks of close support, then hand over to the owner named in step 2.
HR ownerFiori developerSupport
Done whenThe pilot division has set and approved its goals in the app, errors stay under the agreed level for two weeks, and support has a named owner.

What the prototype has, and where it lives for real

The rule: existing systems keep what they already own, and the new database holds only what nothing else does. Entity names come from the standard SuccessFactors APIs and must be checked against your tenant.

Goals: title, measure, dates, statusSuccessFactorsGoal Management goal entity for the plan (Goal_<planId>), plan templateRead and write
Progress percentageSuccessFactorsPercent-complete field on the goal; update history in the app database if the plan does not keep oneRead and write
WeightsSuccessFactors or appDepends on the plan templateGoal weight field when the plan has weights switched on; otherwise a table in the app databaseRead and write
Cascade, contributors, push downSuccessFactors appSuccessFactors goal alignment where it exists; links it cannot hold go in the app databaseRead and write

Best practice to hold the line on

Security and identity

  • One sign-in for both apps; the service trusts the token, never a header from the browser.
  • Calls to SuccessFactors carry the signed-in person, so SuccessFactors enforces its own permissions.
  • Secrets live in the platform's store, not in the app or the repository.
  • Every write names who did it, when, and from which role.

Data integrity

  • Rules run in the service. The screens only show them.
  • One system of record per field, written down in the data map.
  • Weights are whole numbers, never over 100 in total, checked on save.
  • Nothing is deleted. Changes are versions that can be traced.

Speed and resilience

  • Read people and org in bulk and cache them; do not call SuccessFactors per screen.
  • Retries with limits, and a plain message when SuccessFactors is down.
  • Goal lists page their results.
  • Targets to agree: list under two seconds, saves under one.

Delivery

  • One build for every environment; only settings differ.
  • Automated tests gate each move from development to quality to production.
  • Changes to the database schema ship with the code that needs them.
  • Release outside goal-setting deadlines, with a way back.

People, language, access

  • Arabic is a first-class language: right-to-left reviewed by a native speaker, not translated by script alone.
  • Keyboard and screen-reader checks against WCAG 2.1 AA.
  • Phone and tablet widths tested on real devices.

Privacy and compliance

  • No real employee data in the sandbox or in test systems.
  • Check data location and retention with legal, including Qatar's personal data privacy law and company policy.
  • Keep the activity log to what is needed, and say how long it is kept.

What this page rests on

Built and checked: both apps run in a test Fiori launchpad, with navigation between them, goal creation, weights and the English and Arabic switch. Not built: the goals service, the database and the SuccessFactors connection. Entity and field names are the standard ones and need checking in your tenant's API Center. Durations are planning ranges, not commitments.
